query: What signals suggest a support ticket will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: ticket_category
per_column.rationale: Category (bug vs how-to vs incident) is knowable at intake and plausibly drives resolution time; a legitimate feature outside the focus.

per_column.name: product_area
per_column.rationale: Which component the ticket touches is available up front and different areas have systematically different resolution durations.

per_column.name: reported_severity_signal
per_column.rationale: Severity as reported in the description is an intake-time signal correlated with effort; not a restatement of resolution_minutes.

per_column.name: business_deadline_pressure
per_column.rationale: Stated urgency/deadline is knowable at report time and can influence prioritization and thus resolution time.

per_column.name: affected_user_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope of impact (single user vs whole tenant) is derivable from the ticket text and predictive of triage effort and duration.

per_column.name: environment_scope
per_column.rationale: Whether prod vs staging is affected is an intake-time attribute plausibly linked to handling speed and complexity.

per_column.name: root_cause_type
per_column.rationale: Root cause is typically established during/after investigation, not at intake; it co-occurs with the resolution process and risks leaking the outcome.

per_column.name: regression_after_change
per_column.rationale: Whether the issue followed a recent change can be stated in the report and is a plausible pre-resolution predictor; borderline but often knowable at intake.

per_column.name: reproducibility
per_column.rationale: Reproducibility (consistent vs intermittent) is a diagnostic property described early and strongly correlated with debugging effort/time.

judge.rationale: Most added columns are semantically distinct intake-time signals (category, product area, severity, urgency, scope, environment, reproducibility) that lie outside resolution_minutes and plausibly carry predictive signal beyond the original priority/channel/agent columns. root_cause_type is flagged as leakage because it is usually determined through the resolution process itself rather than known before the outcome. As a set they offer strong, non-redundant predictive leverage, so utility is high but not maximal due to one leaking column and some overlap with existing priority.
